chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm and Ibn Fazzal together, said:

We asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about Al-Fuqqa' (a fermented drink), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is forbidden, and it is an unknown wine, and in it is the legal penalty (Hadd) of the wine drinker.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Al-Fuqqa' and is it considered wine?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the status of *Al-Fuqqa’*, a specific fermented beverage, by declaring it *Haram* and categorizing it as *Khamr* despite its lack of widespread recognition. This classification is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it subjects the drink to the standard *Hadd* (fixed legal penalty) for wine, emphasizing that the substance's intoxicating nature, rather than its name or fame, determines its legal ruling. The hadith underscores the principle that any fermented drink causing intoxication falls under the prohibition of wine, aligning with the broader Quranic mandate to avoid intoxicants.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jahm and Ibn Fazzal both together said,
‘We asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about the fermented drink. So heasws said: ‘It is an unknown wine, and with regards to it is a legal penalty (Hadd) of the wine drinker’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm and ibn Faddal all have said the following: “We asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about al-Fuqa’.
He (the Imam) said, ‘It is unlawful, it is an unknown wine and its penalty is the same as that which is for wine.”’
